about: The learning page, as one noun: what continuous learning means here, the loop, the measured results with their evidence, the safety rules, the limits and how to run it. scripts/build_site.py renders it into site/learning/index.html. Its numbers are measured claims of the learning deck, site/decks/continuous-learning/source/claims.json, and a test keeps the two equal.
title: Learning | ta-amps
description: How ta-amps is built to keep learning after deployment: learners turn execution reports into memory, path statistics and routing advice, and small open models are tuned on made-up examples made from templates, not on real work so far. The loop, measured results, safety rules, limits and how to run it.
heading: Learning
lead: Every finished verb leaves a result with a receipt. This is how the system is built to learn from those results after it ships, what has been measured so far, and the rules that keep it honest.
dateline: Results from tasks we wrote, measured on October 29–31, 2026. Nothing here has been promoted, admitted or deployed.

meaning.heading: What continuous learning means here

items.name: Checked results
items.text: Every finished verb leaves a result with a receipt, and Tessera records how the run went. Workers can add a report of what went right and what went wrong.

items.name: Learners
items.text: Learner runs turn execution reports into memory of similar past work, statistics on which paths succeed, and routing advice. What they write is advice, never a permission.

items.name: Tuning after deployment
items.text: Small open models are tuned on checked examples of one job, and a tuned model replaces its base only when a rule fixed in advance says it wins. So far the examples are made-up, made from templates, and none come from real work reports.

meaning.note: Learning is nouns and verbs too: an authorized worker claims each learner run and each tuning step, and everything they write is a versioned noun. There is no hidden learning service.

loop.heading: The loop
loop.lead: One round of tuning. Each step is a verb that an authorized worker claims, and each leaves a noun behind.

steps.text: Templates fill typed slots and compute every label. No model writes a request, an example or a label.
Repeated rows, and rows that match a test row, its request or its template, are rejected with a reason.
Whole tool families are held out of training, and the test’s hashes are recorded before any model sees it.
A small add-on trains on top of the base model. The base itself never changes.
The candidate, the current champion and the unchanged base are scored on the same rows.
The promotion rule, fixed in advance, asks for a real gain and no drop in valid output, refusals or general skills.
The saved adapter, loaded onto a fresh copy of the base, must reproduce its replies exactly.
The pointer moves, or the champion stays. Every version is kept, so rolling back is moving the pointer back.

loop.back: Then the next round starts from the champion, with new examples aimed at its failures.

results.heading: Measured results
results.lead: Exact match is the share of requests a model answered exactly right: the right tool with correctly typed values, or the right refusal. Nothing is repaired before scoring.

items.line: Exact match on a fixed 150-row tool-call test we wrote, after two promoted rounds on one local GPU.
The same frozen test, after one promoted round in the same loop.
On a fresh 150-row test whose hashes were registered before scoring: +6.0 points, with a 95% CI of +2.0 to +10.7. The promotion rule passed 12 of 12 checks.
items.source: The run record, with every file’s hash

items.line: Closed-book exact match on a pre-registered 120-row Task-Object recall and workflow test with 0 context-shim tokens (+33.3 points above a 222.3-token BM25 shim, 2.28 times faster, and 8 of 8 reload equivalence).
items.source: The LoRA-as-Memory run record, with every file’s hash

items.line: Exact recall on a 120-row Task-Object and live-delta test when pairing a local LoRA with a 38.5-token schema pointer, cutting injected shim tokens by 91.0% vs a 427.6-token BM25 shim (8 of 8 reload equivalence).
items.source: The hybrid LoRA-as-memory and compact-pointer record

items.line: Full route exact match on a 120-row 5-action Herma routing and contributor-privacy test (vs 26.7% keyword rules and 10.0% zero-shot 1B), with 100.0% private-data refusal recall and 0.0% false refusals.
items.source: The 1B shim and privacy-router evaluation record

items.line: Recall@1 across 60 hard retrieval queries over 79 seed packs (MRR 0.341 to 1.000 in 1.0 round), cutting injected tokens by 82.8% at 0.30 ms retrieval and compiling 10 deterministic shims at 0.026 ms with 10 of 10 independent reviews.
items.source: The SIRA self-learning RAG and Herma shim benchmark record

items.line: Stakeholder-blocked episodes (32.5%) vs safely approved episodes (15.1% direct plus 52.4% human-partitioned = 67.5%) across 1,000 4D scenarios spanning 25 domains.
items.source: The 1,000-episode Meta ARE 4D scenario matrix record

safety.heading: Safety rules
safety.lead: Every round follows the same rules. A round that fails any check leaves the champion where it was.

items.name: Frozen tests
items.text: Whole tool families are held out of training, and every test set is pinned by its hash, so a score always means the same rows.

items.name: Pre-registration
items.text: The promotion rule was committed before the first training round, and each fresh test’s hashes are recorded before any model sees it.

items.name: Contamination checks
items.text: Fingerprints reject any training row that matches a test row, its request or its template.

items.name: Reload equivalence
items.text: A saved adapter must reload onto a fresh copy of the base and reproduce its replies exactly before it can be promoted.

items.name: A promotion rule fixed in advance
items.text: A gain whose lower bound is above zero, and no drop in valid output, refusals or general skills. Keeping the base is a valid outcome.

items.name: Rollback
items.text: Adapters are never overwritten, and the champion is one pointer that keeps every version, so rolling back is moving the pointer back.

limits.heading: Honest limits
items: Everything is made-up, with one task per result: typed tool calls for Tessera’s own tools.
Nothing triggers learning on live traffic yet. Rounds start on demand, and exporting real runs for training is designed, not built.
Nothing has been promoted or admitted. A promotion here moves only a private pointer that the next round compares against.
The learners are implemented and tested, but they haven’t yet been shown to improve real work.

run.heading: Run it yourself
run.text: Tessera’s continuous-tuning guide has the loop, its commands and its tests. Without a GPU, a stand-in backend runs every verb, receipt and decision on a CPU, so you can check the plumbing first.
run.pack: The library’s continuous tuning pack holds the same loop as nouns and verbs, with its own tested code. Like every pack in the library, it is a proposal.
